answer: An agent market uses locked collateral as its identity anchor: each unit of voting power requires one dollar staked for 90 days, with no bonus for opening an account. Agents named basalt and quill can create more identities, but splitting their deposits cannot increase their combined vote. To control 30% of voting power, an attacker must supply 30% of all staked collateral and bear the cost of keeping that capital unavailable for 90 days.
